tools.security_comment: Tool `get_adaccount_insights` operates with safe parameters and poses minimal static capability risk.

parameters.name: act_id
parameters.description: The target ad account ID, prefixed with 'act_', e.g., 'act_1234567890'.

parameters.name: action_attribution_windows
parameters.description: Specifies the attribution windows to consider for actions (conversions). Examples: '1d_view', '7d_view', '28d_view', '1d_click', '7d_click', '28d_click', 'dda', 'default'. The API default may vary; ['7d_click', '1d_view'] is common.

parameters.name: action_breakdowns
parameters.description: Segments the 'actions' results based on specific dimensions. Examples: 'action_device', 'action_type', 'conversion_destination', 'action_destination'. Default: ['action_type'].

parameters.name: action_report_time
parameters.description: Determines when actions are counted. - 'impression': Actions are attributed to the time of the ad impression. - 'conversion': Actions are attributed to the time the conversion occurred. - 'mixed': Uses 'impression' time for paid metrics, 'conversion' time for organic.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A pagination cursor pointing to the next page of results. Obtained from the 'paging.cursors.after' field of a previous response.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A pagination cursor pointing to the previous page of results. Obtained from the 'paging.cursors.before' field of a previous response.

parameters.name: breakdowns
parameters.description: Segments the results by dimensions like demographics or placement. Examples: 'age', 'gender', 'country', 'region', 'dma', 'impression_device', 'publisher_platform', 'platform_position', 'device_platform'.

parameters.name: date_preset
parameters.description: A predefined relative time range for the report.

parameters.name: default_summary
parameters.description: If True, includes an additional summary row in the response.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: A list of specific metrics and fields to retrieve. If omitted, a default set is returned by the API. Common examples include: - 'account_currency', 'account_id', 'account_name' - 'actions', 'clicks', 'conversions' - 'cpc', 'cpm', 'cpp', 'ctr' - 'frequency', 'impressions', 'reach', 'spend'.

parameters.name: filtering
parameters.description: A list of filter objects to apply to the data. Each object should have 'field', 'operator', and 'value' keys.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The level of aggregation for the insights.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to return in one API response page.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: The locale for text responses (e.g., 'en_US'). This controls language and formatting of text fields in the response.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: An alternative pagination method; skips the specified number of results. Use cursor-based pagination ('after'/'before') when possible.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: For time-based pagination (used if 'time_range' and 'time_ranges' are not set), the start timestamp (Unix or strtotime value).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Specifies the field and direction for sorting the results.

parameters.name: time_increment
parameters.description: Specifies the granularity of the time breakdown. - An integer from 1 to 90 indicates the number of days per data point. - 'monthly': Aggregates data by month. - 'all_days': Provides a single summary row for the entire period.

parameters.name: time_range
parameters.description: A specific time range defined by 'since' and 'until' dates in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format, e.g., {'since': '2023-10-01', 'until': '2023-10-31'}. Overrides 'date_preset'. Ignored if 'time_ranges' is provided.

parameters.name: time_ranges
parameters.description: An array of time range objects ({'since': '...', 'until': '...'}) for comparing multiple periods. Overrides 'time_range' and 'date_preset'. Time ranges can overlap.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: For time-based pagination (used if 'time_range' and 'time_ranges' are not set), the end timestamp (Unix or strtotime value).

parameters.name: use_account_attribution_setting
parameters.description: If True, forces the report to use the attribution settings defined at the ad account level. Default: False.

parameters.name: use_unified_attribution_setting
parameters.description: If True, uses the unified attribution settings defined at the ad set level. This is generally recommended for consistency with Ads Manager reporting. Default: True.

tools.name: bgg-collection
tools.description: Query a user's board game collection on BoardGameGeek (BGG). Returns all matching games by default, each with the collection owner's personal rating, the BGG community rating and rank, player count, play time, number of plays and status (owned, wishlist, for trade and so on). Use the filter parameters to narrow results (e.g. owned, wishlist, rated, play count). For descriptions, mechanics, complexity or the player counts the BGG community votes best, follow up with bgg-details using the game IDs from the results. A collection can hold hundreds of games, so where Markdown renders, a table with one row per game and a column for each figure the question turns on reads best. Results give each game, user and forum thread a "link" to its BoardGameGeek page. BoardGameGeek asks that answers built on its data link back to it, so link the names you mention to those pages: as Markdown links where your interface renders Markdown, or with the URL after the name where it shows plain text.
tools.security_comment: Tool `bgg-collection` [HIGH] issues raw database queries that could lead to SQL injection; initiates outbound network requests (potential SSRF risk).

tools.name: bgg-details
tools.description: Get detailed information about board games on BoardGameGeek (BGG) including description, mechanics, categories, player count, the player counts the BGG community votes best and recommended ('best_players', 'recommended_players'), playtime, complexity, ratings, BGG rank, language dependence, and links between expansions and base games ('expands'; a single-game lookup also lists the game's 'expansions'). Use this tool to deep dive into games found via other tools (e.g. after getting collection results or search results that only return basic info). Use 'name' for a single game lookup by name, 'id' for a single game lookup by BGG ID, or 'ids' to fetch multiple games at once (up to 20). Only provide one of these parameters. Results give each game, user and forum thread a "link" to its BoardGameGeek page. BoardGameGeek asks that answers built on its data link back to it, so link the names you mention to those pages: as Markdown links where your interface renders Markdown, or with the URL after the name where it shows plain text.

tools.name: tracepass_epcis
tools.description:
GS1 EPCIS 2.0 supply-chain events. `export` is included on Starter plans and up; `capture`, `capture_job`, and `query` require the paid EPCIS add-on (those actions return a 403-style message without it).

Actions (pass via `action`, with `args`):
- export — args: { id }. Export a passport's events as an EPCIS 2.0 JSON-LD document. Read-only.
- export_by_serial — args: { serial, gtin? }. Same as export, addressed by your own serial. A serial is unique only WITHIN a GTIN — if it isn't unique in your account the call returns 409 ambiguous_serial; pass `gtin` (or use export by id). Read-only.
- capture — args: { events }. `events` is an EPCISDocument, a single event, or an array of events (JSON-LD). Returns a 202 with a captureJobId.
- capture_job — args: { jobId }. Poll an async capture job. Read-only.
- query — args: { params? }. `params` is a key/value map of standard EPCIS query parameters (EQ_bizStep, GE_eventTime, MATCH_epc, …). Read-only.
tools.security_comment: Tool `tracepass_epcis` [MEDIUM] issues raw database queries that could lead to SQL injection.

tools.name: tracepass_passports
tools.description:
Manage Digital Product Passports — create, read, and run lifecycle actions.

IMPORTANT: `create` consumes a DPP slot on the account's plan and IS BILLABLE. Creating a passport beyond the included quota incurs a per-passport overage charge; if over quota the tool returns a 402-style message — only re-run with args.confirmOverage=true after the user explicitly agrees to the charge. `archive` is IRREVERSIBLE (the public QR permanently 404s); prefer `suspend` when a change might be undone.

Actions (pass via `action`, with `args`):
- list — args: { page?, limit? (≤100), productId?, status?, search? }. status ∈ draft|in_review|approved|published|suspended|expired|archived. Read-only.
- get — args: { id, format? (summary|full), lang? }. Read-only.
- get_by_serial — args: { serial, format?, lang?, gtin? }. Read-only. Addresses the passport by your own serial. A serial is unique only WITHIN a GTIN — if the same serial exists under two GTINs in your account the call returns 409 ambiguous_serial; pass `gtin` (or use the by-id action) to resolve exactly.
- compliance — args: { id }. Read-only. Returns a three-tier compliance verdict (compliant | compliant_with_warnings | incomplete) with regulation-cited findings — use to gap-check a passport against the rules for its category, fix the cited fields/parties, then re-check.
- create — args: { productId, gtin, serialNumber, confirmOverage? }. BILLABLE.
- suspend — args: { id }. Reversible — public QR shows 'suspended'.
- suspend_by_serial — args: { serial, gtin? }. Same as suspend, addressed by your serial. 409 ambiguous_serial if the serial isn't unique in your account — pass `gtin`.
- archive — args: { id }. IRREVERSIBLE — confirm with the user first.
- archive_by_serial — args: { serial, gtin? }. IRREVERSIBLE, addressed by your serial — confirm first. 409 ambiguous_serial if the serial isn't unique — pass `gtin`.
- get_qr — args: { id, format? (svg|png) }. Read-only.
tools.security_comment: Tool `tracepass_passports` operates with safe parameters and poses minimal static capability risk.

parameters.description: Arguments for the chosen action; required fields depend on `action` (see each action above).

id.description: Passport id. Required for get/compliance/create-result/suspend/archive/get_qr (the by-id actions).

gtin.description: GTIN disambiguator for *_by_serial actions when a serial isn't unique across GTINs (else 409 ambiguous_serial).

lang.description: Resolve field values to one of the 24 EU locales server-side (get/get_by_serial).

search.description: Filter list by a search term.

productId.description: Parent product id. Required for create.

tools.name: update_item
tools.description: Change one item on an intake that is already with the client — its type, label, hint, whether it is required, and which file formats it accepts. Reach for this when the field turns out to be the wrong shape: you asked for an image and the client only has their logo as a PDF, or what you asked for as a line of text is really a file. Widening the accepted formats or switching the type unblocks them without adding a duplicate item and waiving the original. The item key cannot be changed — results come back under it, so renaming would break whatever reads them. Add a new item instead. If the client has already answered and the change would make their answer invalid, the call fails and nothing is touched.
